PJ01.title: First run - a hive with no projects at all
PJ01.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 (static, and the limitation is stated below). THIS ONE IS CLEAN, recorded as a real result rather than hunted for a defect: renderEmptyState DISTINGUISHES the two empty states that PJ8 had to be fixed for elsewhere - totalProjects === 0 renders four actionable template tiles ('Pick a flavour. Each one comes with industry-standard scope items you can tweak'), while 'some exist but none match the filter' renders a separate hint pointing at clearing the search or switching to All. The Plain-Read verdict degrades honestly too: tone='empty', 'No projects yet', with a next action naming BOTH routes (+ New Project, or the AI text bootstrap), and the stat cards read 'No projects in active status' tagged IDLE/grey rather than a bare 0. LIMITATION, stated rather than papered over: this was verified by reading the branches, NOT by walking a live zero-project hive, because all three seeded hives hold 12 projects each. That is the AHK3 class again - the first-run state every new customer begins in has no fixture. Lower severity than the Asset Hub instance (the branches here are simple and provably distinct, where AH1's cold-start hid two real defects), so it is logged rather than treated as blocking, and the seeder gap is the honest reason W is credited on two states rather than a live walk.

PJ02.title: Create a project - code generation, dates, budget
PJ02.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE RACE IS SAFE, checked first: generate_project_code does MAX(seq)+1 and the client then INSERTs, which is a read-then-write - but projects_code_per_hive is a UNIQUE index on (hive_id, project_code) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, so two concurrent creates collide with 23505 rather than producing a duplicate. The CON-2026-001 x3 rows are across DIFFERENT hives, which the per-hive index correctly allows. THE REAL DEFECT is the interaction between that PARTIAL index and soft delete. The generator scans 'WHERE deleted_at IS NULL', so deleting a project immediately frees its code. Proven live in a rolled-back transaction: soft-delete SHD-2026-001 (live count 1 -> 0), generator returns SHD-2026-001 again, a new project takes it - and RESTORING the original then fails with 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint projects_code_per_hive'. WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: mig ...026, written earlier in this same arc, made restore a first-class supervisor-gated AUDITED operation. So the arc had just made prominent a path that can fail with a raw 23505 and no explanation. Finding this was a direct consequence of having built that. FIXED BY STOPPING THE REUSE, not by patching restore, for the same reason the change-order work settled on: the code is an IDENTITY THAT LEAVES THE SYSTEM - printed on Project and Reliability Reports, quoted in change orders, referenced in sign-off documents. Two projects sharing SHD-2026-001 in the historical record is worse than a confusing error; one is recoverable, the other means two documents cannot be told apart. mig ...029 drops the deleted_at filter from the generator's scan so the sequence only moves forward. The partial UNIQUE INDEX is deliberately LEFT ALONE - it is what makes soft-delete possible at all; the fix just stops the generator walking into the overlap. VERIFIED: generator now returns SHD-2026-002 with SHD-2026-001 soft-deleted, and the restore SUCCEEDS. SECOND PERSONA, added because the SHALLOW-W GUARD REFUSED to credit this journey on one - and that refusal is the only reason the next defect surfaced. Probing as an ordinary worker found: a worker CAN create a project (including a CAPEX one), and - the real find - a worker could SET budget_php to PHP 5,000,000 on it. PJ9's mig ...024 closed the READ path and never touched the WRITE path: information_schema still showed authenticated and anon holding INSERT and UPDATE on the column. So a worker could not SEE any budget and could WRITE one. The page-level _budgetReadable guard I had added stops the UI doing it, and a page-level guard is precisely what PJK3 exists to reject. FIXED (mig ...030): INSERT/UPDATE revoked on the column by the same mechanism as SELECT (drop the table-wide grant, re-grant every other column from a GENERATED list), plus set_project_budget() as the sanctioned supervisor-only write - because revoking without providing a path would have broken supervisors, who legitimately set budgets in both the wizard and the edit form. Both page paths rewired: the edit form applies the budget after the row write, and the wizard after creation, each reporting a refusal as 'the project saved, the budget did not' rather than implying total failure. VERIFIED: worker INSERT with a budget -> permission denied; worker creating a project WITHOUT one -> still works; worker calling the RPC -> refused with a reason; SUPERVISOR via the RPC -> {ok:true, budget_php:2500000}.

PJ03.title: Scope items: add, sequence, set predecessors
PJ03.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE EXISTING DATA IS CLEAN: 78 of 90 items carry predecessors, and 0 point outside their own project. So the seeded DAG is well-formed and this is not a live corruption. WHAT IS UNCONSTRAINED: predecessors is JSONB, which cannot carry a foreign key, and nothing else validates it. Probed live as a worker, all three ACCEPTED - a two-item CYCLE (each naming the other), a CROSS-PROJECT predecessor (an item depending on an item in a different project), and a PHANTOM predecessor (a uuid that exists nowhere). THE ENGINE'S BEHAVIOUR IS ASYMMETRIC, and that asymmetry IS the finding. prescriptive.py handles a cycle honestly - networkx.find_cycle() raises and it returns a stated cycle_warning, so the schedule degrades to 'no critical path' with a reason rather than a wrong answer. But the DAG is built with `for pred in predecessors: if pred in by_id: G.add_edge(...)`, so a predecessor that is not one of THIS project's items is SILENTLY SKIPPED. No warning, no count. SO THE IMPACT IS NOT A WRONG CRITICAL PATH - it is a DROPPED DEPENDENCY. A planner records 'task B waits on task A', the UI accepts it, and the schedule quietly does not honour it. The dependency looks stored and is not acted on, which is the 'a string is not an announcement until it reaches a user' shape applied to a graph edge. FIX/GATE OPEN, and the shape is small because the channel already exists: count the predecessors that could not be resolved and report them alongside cycle_warning, so the pane can say which dependencies were ignored. The engine already proves it is willing to say 'your graph is malformed' - it just does not say it for this case. FIXED 2026-07-28. prescriptive.py now COLLECTS every predecessor it cannot resolve and returns them as unresolved_predecessors, on the SUCCESS path as well as the two error paths - and the success path is the one that matters, because a schedule can compute perfectly well while quietly ignoring a dependency the planner recorded. Reporting only on the error paths would have left the common case exactly as silent as before. The CPM pane now names the count and says plainly that the schedule below ignores those dependencies. VERIFIED against the engine directly: two items where B depends on A (valid) plus a phantom uuid and a foreign-project id - the critical path still computes correctly (A -> B, 5 days) AND both unresolvable predecessors are reported. Before, they vanished. NOT CHANGED, deliberately: predecessors remains jsonb with no constraint, and a cycle is still handled the way it already was (networkx.find_cycle raises, the engine returns cycle_warning and refuses to publish a critical path). Adding a database constraint to a jsonb array is not available, and the honest alternative - report what could not be honoured - is what the module was already doing for cycles. This just extends the same courtesy to the other malformed case.

PJ04.title: Change order: raise -> approve / reject / cancel (G5 - never walked)
PJ04.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 as a real WORKER (SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated + request.jwt.claims), every probe inside a transaction that ROLLED BACK. THE WALK REFUTED MY OWN GROUND FINDING, which is the most useful thing it did. G4 claimed 'one permissive ALL policy per table means any active member can approve a change order'. I had asserted that from the POLICY layer alone and it is WRONG: wh_guard_supervisor_approval() is a TRIGGER over six tables and project_change_orders is one of them - I had even written that list into the AHK1 gate label earlier in the same session and still did not check it here. Measured: approve -> BLOCKED, reject -> BLOCKED (the AH3 clause working), edit an APPROVED CO's cost -> BLOCKED ('remove signed-off work'). Recall the disposition before declaring a bug. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is sharper than what I guessed: the guard protects the approval ACT and signed-off work, and nothing protects the CONTENT or the EXISTENCE of a request awaiting review. Proven live - worker Bryan Garcia rewrote worker Wilfredo Malabanan's PENDING change order from PHP 500,000 to PHP 9,999,999 and replaced its scope text, and the row still reads requested_by = Wilfredo Malabanan. A worker can also DELETE a pending CO outright. Combined with G1 (no auth_uid on the table) and G2 (no audit trigger on projects), nothing records that it changed or who changed it: the supervisor approves what they are SHOWN, and what they are shown is editable by anyone in the hive. A FIXTURE WEAKNESS FOUND EN ROUTE: my seeder assigns every CO in a hive the same requested_by (m.rn=2), so the first 'can a worker edit ANOTHER's CO' probe returned UPDATE 0 and looked like a block. It was not - there was simply no other requester's row to match. Inserting one made the tamper succeed immediately. UPDATE 0 is not evidence of a guard; it is the 0-row-write-is-not-an-error lesson in probe form. FIX/GATE still open. FIXED by 20260728000022: a raised change order's COMMERCIAL TERMS are immutable (cost, schedule, scope, title, requester, project, hive) and it cannot be DELETED - cancel instead, so the request stays visible in the amendment trail. Status and the approver fields stay mutable, with wh_guard_supervisor_approval still deciding who may move them. LEGITIMATE CALLERS MEASURED FIRST, because twice in the previous arc the obvious guard would have broken more than the bug: there are exactly THREE update paths on this table in the whole codebase (approveCO/rejectCO/cancelCO), all of which set status plus approver fields and nothing else; there is NO edit-CO path anywhere and NO delete path in any page or edge fn. The terms were already write-once in practice, so making the DATABASE agree breaks zero callers - and immutability is a stronger guarantee than a role check. VERIFIED: worker cost-tamper -> blocked, delete -> blocked, worker cancel -> still allowed, SUPERVISOR APPROVE -> still allowed (UPDATE 1).

PJ06.title: Progress log: submit, acknowledge, dispute
PJ06.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28, three defects, all probed live as an ordinary worker. (1) REWROTE ANOTHER WORKER'S REPORT: set pct_complete=100 and replaced the notes on a log filed by Leandro Marquez, and the row still read reported_by = Leandro Marquez. The record of what a technician said they did now said what somebody else wrote. (2) ACKNOWLEDGED SOMEONE ELSE'S REPORT: acknowledgement is the supervisor's 'I have seen this' signal and any active member could write it - ackLog() sets acknowledged_by = WORKER_NAME with no role check, and wh_guard_supervisor_approval does not cover this table. (3) ACKNOWLEDGED THEIR OWN REPORT - 'Bryan Garcia acked their OWN report as Bryan Garcia'. That is the self-approval class AH3 closed for asset submissions, still open here: the one signal that a supervisor reviewed the work could be manufactured by the person being reviewed. LEGITIMATE CALLERS MEASURED FIRST (fourth time in two arcs that this changed the fix): exactly TWO write paths exist - the INSERT that files a log and the acknowledge UPDATE - and NO edit-log path anywhere. So the content was already write-once in practice and making the database agree breaks nothing. FIXED (mig ...027): a filed report is a RECORD - content immutable, acknowledging is a supervisor act, and nobody may acknowledge their own. VERIFIED all four ways: worker rewrite -> blocked; worker ack -> blocked; SUPERVISOR self-ack -> blocked ('Another supervisor must review it'); supervisor acking someone else -> works. A LIMIT STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the self-check compares worker_name, because project_progress_logs has no auth_uid - six of seven project tables do not. So the guard is as strong as a NAME, which is exactly PJK1's open attribution half.

PJ07.title: Earned Value - is green/amber/red defensible? (EVM / PMBOK)
PJ07.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. MY OWN GROUND NOTE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I judged the client fallback's 'hoursActual * 200' and invented-looking 0.95/0.85 bands WITHOUT reading the implementation it falls back FROM. python-api/projects/diagnostic.py is well-founded: it cites PMI PMBOK 7th ed. (Measurement) and AACE International RP 80R-13, states every formula in its docstring (PV/EV/AC/SV/CV/SPI/CPI), attributes the green/amber/red bands to AACE EV interpretation guidance rather than inventing them, and REFUSES when inputs are missing - {available:false, reason:'Requires budget_php + start_date + end_date'} - which is precisely the refusal path PJK2 asks for. DEFAULT_LABOR_RATE_PHP_PER_HOUR = 200 is a documented DEFAULT PROXY with a stated upgrade path ('Phase 5 will pull from worker_profiles') and is overridable per call. Recall the disposition before declaring a bug - twice in this arc now. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is narrower and sharper: (1) THE OVERRIDE IS DEAD. project-manager.html never passes labor_rate_php_per_hour - 0 matches in the file - so the parameter exists, is documented, and is never supplied. Every project on the platform is costed at PHP 200/hour regardless of trade or region, and CPI is EV/AC, so CPI is off by exactly the ratio of the real rate to 200. (2) TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE METRIC. clientRollup() re-implements EVM in the browser with the same constants and the same bands but NO citation, so the standard-citing version and the unattributed copy can drift apart with nothing detecting it. (3) THEY ALREADY DISAGREE. Both weight pct_complete by estimated_hours, but the client wraps it in Math.round() and the server keeps the float. EV = BAC x (pct/100), so rounding pct to an integer moves EV by up to 0.5% of BAC - on the seeded PHP 1,850,000 project that is about PHP 9,250 of Earned Value, and it is the CLIENT number a supervisor sees when the edge fn has not answered. FIX/GATE open: the shape is a single source of truth for the bands + rate (register the formula in canonical/formula_contracts.json as AH7's Action Priority was), the page passing a real rate, and a gate asserting the client fallback cannot diverge from the cited implementation. FIXED 2026-07-28 by DELETING the duplicate rather than patching its rounding. The client no longer computes Earned Value at all - the same discipline renderCpm already had, and PJ8 confirmed is the better one: a cost figure that silently disagrees with the cited engine is worse than no figure, especially one that feeds a client-facing report. The rest of clientRollup (progress %, hours, counts) is untouched and still serves the page when functions are unavailable. AND THE EMPTY STATE WAS SPLIT, because the fix exposed a second lie: renderBudget told a supervisor to 'add a budget, start date and end date' even when all three existed and the rollup had simply not answered - sending them to re-enter data that was already there. The engine reports {available:false, reason:...} when inputs are genuinely missing, so its ABSENCE means the computation did not run, which is now said plainly. Same shape as PJ8's critical-path fix. REGISTERED as formula evm_cpi_spi_pmbok with partial_variant=true, and the partial_reason is the honest one: the formulas and bands are the STANDARD ones (PMBOK 7 / AACE RP 80R-13), what is partial is AC - actual cost is an hours x rate PROXY because the platform has no cost ledger, the rate defaults to PHP 200/hour, and MEASURED, no caller ever passes the override that exists. So CPI remains wrong by exactly the ratio of the real rate to 200 until a rate source is wired. That is now recorded in the contract where an auditor can see it, rather than buried in a default. STILL OPEN: wiring a real labour rate (the code's own TODO says worker_profiles).

PJ08.title: Critical path - what decides that a task may slip?
PJ08.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE SERVER IMPLEMENTATION IS SOUND, and saying so is half the value of the walk: python-api/projects/prescriptive.py cites PMBOK 7th ed. §6.5.2.2 (Critical Path Method) and AACE 24R-03 (Forensic Schedule Analysis), uses networkx.dag_longest_path() rather than hand-rolled graph code, documents the forward/backward pass (ES/EF/LF/LS, slack = LS - ES, critical = slack 0), and carries real refusal paths - no items returns an empty critical path, and a missing networkx returns a stated cycle_warning instead of guessing. Its own docstring records that the PREVIOUS hand-rolled TS version silently miscomputed cycles and that networkx.find_cycle() now raises cleanly. That is the AHK2/PJK2 bar being met. A GOOD CONTRAST WITH PJ7, and it sharpens that finding: the client NEVER recomputes the critical path - 0 matches for any client-side CPM - it only reads _progress.critical_path. So the same page handles its two computed numbers with two different disciplines: the schedule verdict has ONE implementation, while Earned Value has a second, uncited copy in the browser that already diverges on rounding. THE DEFECT FOUND: an absence rendered as a VERDICT. renderCpm defaulted to {item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {}} whenever the rollup was unavailable, so every task drew as NON-critical with ZERO slack. That is a positive answer where there should be none, and a self-contradictory one - zero slack is normally exactly what MAKES a task critical. Same shape as the is_anomaly defect in the Asset Hub arc. FIXED: the pane now says the critical path could not be computed and that nothing is therefore marked critical or slack-free, rather than quietly asserting a clean schedule.

PJ09.title: Budget: can a non-supervisor read it anyway? (G6)
PJ09.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. G6 CONFIRMED LIVE, and it is a UI-only gate on commercially sensitive data. renderBudget() tells a non-supervisor 'Budget visibility is restricted to supervisors' while projects_hive_rw grants every active member SELECT. Probed as worker Bryan Garcia: read budget_php straight off the table - CAP-2026-001 PHP 1,850,000 and CON-2026-001 PHP 280,000. The page renders a refusal; the database hands it over. WIDER THAN THE PANE: budget_php is in the MAIN project-list select (line 989) for every user, not just supervisors, and BAC is then computed client-side - so the number is already in the browser of everyone who opens the page, before any pane decides whether to show it. It is also exposed through v_project_truth. LEGITIMATE READERS MEASURED: the page itself (list select + the edit form + the client-side EVM), and two edge fns (project-orchestrator, project-progress) which run service-role and are unaffected by a client-side tightening. FIX/GATE open - the shape that fits this codebase is the one used twice already this session: move the privileged read into a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that checks supervisor role itself, drop budget_php from the client select, and let the edge fns keep their reach. PARTIAL FIX 2026-07-28 (mig ...023), and the partiality is stated deliberately rather than rounded up: get_project_budget() is a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that returns budget_php + the EVM dates ONLY to an active supervisor of that hive, using the same predicate as wh_guard_supervisor_approval so authority lives in one place. Verified both ways - supervisor gets PHP 1,850,000; worker gets {ok:false, reason:'not a supervisor'} with a stated detail rather than a silent null, so a refusal is not mistaken for 'this project has no budget'. THE HOLE IS NOT YET CLOSED and it would be dishonest to mark this journey done: the RPC adds a SANCTIONED path, it does not remove the unsanctioned one. A worker can still db.from('projects').select('budget_php') because RLS is row-level. Closing it needs three things together, which is why it is the next slice rather than a quick follow-on: REVOKE SELECT (budget_php) ON projects FROM authenticated (Postgres column privileges - the only mechanism that can withhold ONE column of a readable row), drop budget_php from the page's list select at line 989 and route renderBudget/clientRollup through the RPC, and decide what v_project_truth should expose, since it carries the column too. The edge fns are unaffected either way - both run service-role. BLAST RADIUS WIDENED 2026-07-28, and it turned the closure into a PRODUCT FORK rather than an engineering task. project-report.html renders 'Budget: PHP X' and computes BAC with NO supervisor gate of any kind (no isSupervisor, no HIVE_ROLE check anywhere in the file) - it only requires sign-in. It also feeds the budget into the AI companion context. And it reads v_project_truth with select('*'), as does project-orchestrator. SO A REVOKE WOULD BREAK IT: v_project_truth is security_invoker, so revoking SELECT(budget_php) on the base table propagates to the view, and a select('*') against a column the caller cannot read fails outright. project-orchestrator is service_role and unaffected; project-report is a CLIENT page and would break for supervisors too. THE REAL QUESTION IS NOT TECHNICAL. project-manager says budget is supervisor-only; project-report is a printable, signed-off client document whose own meta description is 'cost vs budget' and whose footer reads 'By signing below, the parties acknowledge...'. Those are two contradictory intents about who may see the figure, and which one is correct decides whether I gate the report or instead remove project-manager's false claim. That is Ian's call, not mine - putting a supervisor gate on a client sign-off document would change what the document IS. CLOSED 2026-07-28 (mig ...024) after Ian chose supervisor-only EVERYWHERE. THE COLUMN-LEVEL REVOKE ALONE WAS A NO-OP, and only a live check caught it: Postgres tests TABLE-level privilege first, so while GRANT SELECT ON projects TO authenticated stood, REVOKE SELECT (budget_php) changed nothing - column_privileges still listed authenticated on the column and a worker still read the figure. The working mechanism is to DROP the table-wide grant and re-GRANT the allowed columns explicitly, with the list GENERATED from information_schema rather than typed, since one missed column is an instant 42501 on a page that used to work. v_project_truth also had to lose the column: it is security_invoker, so a revoked base column would have made every select('*') against the view fail - and project-report.html and project-orchestrator both do exactly that. MY FIRST DRAFT OF THAT VIEW WAS WRITTEN FROM MEMORY AND WAS BADLY WRONG - it omitted all EIGHT correlated subqueries the pages depend on (item_count, items_done, estimated/actual_total_hours, last_progress_at, approved_change_orders, approved_co_cost_php, link_count), renamed actual_end_at, replaced the project_links-based maintenance_nature with a naive type map, and dropped the status<>'archived' filter. Dumping pg_get_viewdef first is the only reason the applied version is correct - the third time this session that rule has paid for itself. PAGE SIDE: budget_php removed from the shared list select; openDetail's select('*') enumerated explicitly (it would have 42501'd for everyone); the edit form prefills from the RPC and the save path OMITS the key entirely when the caller could not read it, because sending null would ERASE the budget - a blank field means withheld, never zero; clientRollup asks the RPC and simply renders no EVM block without a figure. VERIFIED at the privilege boundary, which is where the claim lives: worker direct read -> permission denied; worker other columns -> fine; worker select('*') on the view -> fine (22 cols, no budget, rollups intact, security_invoker preserved); worker RPC -> refused WITH a reason; supervisor RPC -> PHP 1,850,000. AN INSTRUMENT ERROR EN ROUTE, the third today: my first RPC test failed with 'permission denied' and looked like the fix breaking its own RPC - but the ARGUMENT subquery said WHERE budget_php IS NOT NULL, which runs as the CALLER. The RPC was never at fault. FOLLOW-UP LOGGED, not silently widened: v_project_truth still exposes approved_co_cost_php, also a financial figure readable by any member. Ian's decision covered the BUDGET; expanding it unasked would be scope creep on a security change.

PJ10.title: Roles: assign, remove, and what a role actually gates (G5)
PJ10.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. The G5 fixture made this walkable at all - project_roles went 0 -> 36 rows. THE FINDING: a project role GATES NOTHING. The CHECK allows owner | planner | safety_officer | cost_engineer | reviewer, the rows are loaded, grouped by role and rendered with a count - and no authority anywhere consults them. Every gate on the page keys off isSupervisor(), which reads HIVE_ROLE === 'supervisor' from hive_members: the budget tab, the Acknowledge button, the remove-role control. Nor do any of the three guards I added this session consult a project role (the one grep hit in mig ...026 is a comment listing cascade tables). The only place the concept appears in a decision is project_roles_supervisor_all, the policy saying supervisors may MANAGE roles. WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING MERELY UNUSED: the role VOCABULARY makes a promise the system does not keep. 'safety_officer' and 'cost_engineer' name accountability - a reader reasonably assumes the safety officer is the one who signs something off, or that a cost engineer is who approves a change order's cost impact. Assigning them changes nothing at all. That is the same shape as a trust signal with no producer behind it. NOT FIXED, because the fix is a PRODUCT FORK and not mine to decide: either (a) project roles are informational, a team directory, in which case the naming should stop implying authority, or (b) they are meant to gate - and then the obvious wiring is that a change order's cost impact needs the cost_engineer or a supervisor, and safety-classified scope needs the safety_officer, which is a real design decision about how a plant runs. Recorded for Ian rather than guessed.

PJ11.title: Links to logbook / inventory / marketplace - do they survive deletion?
PJ11.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. project_links is POLYMORPHIC (link_type + link_id across logbook, asset, inventory_item, pm_completion, engineering_calc) and carries exactly ONE foreign key - to `projects`. link_id itself has NO constraint, which is unavoidable for a polymorphic reference and is exactly why it can drift silently. Same class as fault_knowledge.logbook_id. THE DANGLING SCAN LOOKED ALARMING AND THE FIRST READING WAS WRONG: 12 of 12 ASSET links failed to match asset_nodes.id, while logbook 0/9, inventory 0/21 and pm_completion 0/6 were clean. A type-specific total failure is not deletion drift, it is a wrong-table id - and it is: every asset link stores a value like 'asset-9fbe0f6f4022', and all 12 match asset_nodes.LEGACY_ASSET_ID. So three link types use the modern id and one uses the legacy one. WHY NOBODY NOTICED: renderLinked draws a label-only pill - ${l.label || l.link_id} plus a remove button - with NO navigation at all. Nothing ever resolves link_id, so a mismatched id costs nothing today and would break the moment anyone made links clickable. That is the reachable-capability shape in reverse: a stored reference nothing follows. AND IT EXPOSES A GAP IN MY OWN AH11 WORK, which is the most useful thing here: all 12 asset-link LABELS match an asset NAME (0 match a tag), and project_links appears NOWHERE in sync_asset_identity. So renaming an asset leaves the project's linked-items list showing the OLD name, with no id-based way to refresh it since link_id points at a legacy id nothing resolves. AH11 measured the identity spine as five text columns; this is a SIXTH, and it is keyed by NAME rather than TAG, which is why a tag-driven sweep would never have found it. FIX/GATE OPEN, and the shape is known: sync_asset_identity would need the OLD NAME threaded through as well as the old tag (logbook.html's updateAsset has both), and link_id should carry a resolvable asset_nodes.id so the label stops being the only thing holding the reference together.

PJ12.title: Delete a project - what goes with it, and is it recorded? (G2)
PJ12.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THREE MEASURED FACTS. (1) A WORKER COULD SOFT-DELETE ANY PROJECT IN THEIR HIVE. deleteProject() sets deleted_at, the button carries no role check, and neither did the database - projects_hive_rw is a single PERMISSIVE FOR ALL testing only membership. Probed live: an ordinary worker hid SHD-2026-001, a shutdown project they do not own, and every view filters deleted_at IS NULL so it vanishes for everyone. (2) NOTHING RECORDED IT - the G2 ground finding confirmed live: hive_audit_log held ZERO rows for target_type='projects' or any project-named action. A project could disappear and the log could not say it had ever existed, let alone who removed it. (3) A HARD delete cascades to ALL SIX child tables (every FK is ON DELETE CASCADE), and it is currently refused for any project carrying a change order because 20260728000022's immutability trigger fires on the cascade. That is an ACCIDENTAL side effect of a fix aimed at something else. Recorded rather than left to be discovered: nothing legitimate breaks today because the UI only soft-deletes, but a future admin hard-delete WILL fail with a change-order error that reads as unrelated. FIXED (mig ...026): removing or restoring a project is a supervisor act and is recorded either way, with the children counted BEFORE the statement because after a cascade there is nothing left to describe what was lost - the same reason trg_asset_node_delete_audit is a BEFORE trigger. Guarded rather than forbidden, because soft-delete is the intended workflow. VERIFIED: worker soft-delete -> blocked with a plain reason; worker ORDINARY EDIT -> still works (no over-blocking, which is the failure mode a broad guard invites); supervisor delete -> succeeds AND writes the platform's first ever projects audit row: 'Leandro Marquez | delete_project | SHD-2026-001 | 1 COs, 7 items'. The three new actions are registered in hive.html's ACTION_ICON with EN+FIL labels and their valence, so the trail is READABLE rather than a row of unlabelled dots - the exact gap the audit-coverage gate caught earlier today.

PJ13.title: Cross-hive: a foreign project's items / COs cannot leak or be written (G3)
PJ13.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28, and this is the probe that EARNS PJK4 rather than assuming it from the AHK4 analogy. READS ARE CORRECTLY ISOLATED, measured first and worth recording as a real result: as a member of one hive, projects / project_items / project_change_orders all return 0 rows for another hive. WRITES HAD THE PM13 GAP - with MY hive_id and ANOTHER hive's project_id, all three were ACCEPTED: a project_item, a progress log, and a CHANGE ORDER attached to a project the writer cannot even see. An APPROVED change order was refused, but by wh_guard_supervisor_approval on the STATUS, not by anything tenancy-related - worth stating so the next reader does not mistake that for isolation. INSTRUMENT NOTE, and it nearly produced a false clean: my first two probes failed with 23514 (a status enum I got wrong) and 23502 (a NOT NULL I omitted). Neither is 42501. Verify WHAT blocked a write, never merely THAT something did - the same trap AH13 hit on the reliability tables. SEVERITY MEASURED, AND HONESTLY CONTAINED - TODAY. v_project_truth's rollup subqueries (item_count, estimated_total_hours, approved_change_orders, approved_co_cost_php, link_count) carry NO hive filter; they are plain WHERE pi.project_id = p.id. What keeps an injected row out of the VICTIM's numbers is that the view is security_invoker, so those subqueries execute as the READER and RLS hides the foreign row. Proven: injecting an item with 999 estimated hours left the victim's rollup at 7 items / 33.00 est hrs, and the victim could not see the row. FIXED ANYWAY (mig ...025, five RESTRICTIVE parent-hive policies) because that containment rests ENTIRELY on security_invoker staying ON - and earlier the SAME DAY a routine CREATE OR REPLACE silently cleared that exact option from v_sensor_truth, since CREATE VIEW does not carry reloptions forward. One such slip on v_project_truth turns every unfiltered rollup subquery into a cross-tenant read, instantly and silently. Closing it at the WRITE removes the dependence on that option and on every future consumer remembering to be hive-scoped. 0 existing rows violated the new policies, so nothing that exists was rejected. VERIFIED: foreign -parent item and change-order inserts both blocked BY NAME (the policy is named in the error, which is far more diagnosable than the 23514 confusion above), and a legitimate own-hive write still succeeds. GATE validate_project_tenancy, teeth proven by dropping a policy -> FAIL on exactly that table.

PJ14.title: AI: draft lessons + intent modal - grounded and attributable?
PJ14.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. MOSTLY GOOD, and the good parts are worth asserting because they are the pattern other surfaces should copy: the AI draft is NOT auto-saved - it fills a textarea and the toast says 'review and Save lessons to keep it', so a human decides; it REFUSES up front when there are no progress logs to draft from rather than inventing lessons; saveLessons carries an optimistic-concurrency guard on updated_at with the 0-row case handled by reloading (the 0-row-write-is-not-an-error lesson, already applied here); and the AI provenance tag DOES survive the save, because saveLessons spreads _detail.meta rather than replacing it. THE DEFECT IS NARROW AND IS THE AI-ACCOUNTABILITY CLASS INVERTED: aiDraftLessons tags meta._ai_generated_lessons the moment a draft LOADS, and nothing ever compares that to what is finally saved. So a supervisor who drafted with AI, then deleted the text and wrote their own, still got the badge '🤖 AI-drafted on <date>: supervisor edit before sign-off recommended' printed over their own words. AI6 was about AI output attributed to a HUMAN; this is human output attributed to AI. Both misdescribe who is answerable for the text on a document that gets signed. FIXED: the drafted text is remembered, and the badge fields are dropped at save time if what is being written is no longer that draft. The badge now describes what is SAVED rather than what was once loaded. SECOND PERSONA, again forced by the shallow-W guard, and again it is where the real defect was. Neither button is role-gated (aiDraftLessons and saveLessons carry no isSupervisor check, unlike Acknowledge which does) - and beneath them, projects.meta is an unstructured jsonb grab-bag writable by any active member through the table's single PERMISSIVE FOR ALL policy. Probed live as a worker: ONE statement set meta.lessons_learned AND forged _ai_generated_lessons=true on EVERY project in the hive. WHY THAT IS NOT JUST ANOTHER FIELD: meta.lessons_learned renders on project-report.html, the printable document whose own footer reads 'By signing below, the parties acknowledge...'. It is content on a document people SIGN, and the same write forged the badge a reviewer would rely on to know whether a human wrote it. FIXED (mig ...031): only a supervisor may CHANGE meta.lessons_learned; every other meta key stays writable by any member, because meta genuinely is a grab-bag (wizard state, flags, UI prefs) and locking the column would break unrelated writes. VERIFIED: worker writing lessons -> blocked by name; worker writing a different meta key -> still works; SUPERVISOR writing lessons -> works. LEFT OPEN AND STATED: the AI badge itself is not validated, because it is set CLIENT-side and the database cannot tell a truthful badge from a forged one. The honest fix is for the orchestrator to stamp provenance SERVER-side; adding a check here would only catch the careless case and would read as protection that is not there.

PJ18.title: Mobile 390px - approve a CO from the field
PJ18.notes:
MOBILE 390px. Verified the viewport first (browser_resize lies — echoed innerWidth 390 at dpr 0.667 before measuring anything).
FIND 1, and it was not a mobile bug at all: four lines of my own JS comment sat ABOVE <!DOCTYPE html> at the top of the file. They RENDERED as visible text above the page heading — internal notes naming revoked columns and 42501 — and, because a doctype that is not first is discarded, the WHOLE PAGE ran in QUIRKS MODE (measured document.compatMode === 'BackCompat'). Every layout rule on the page was being applied under the old box model, at every viewport. It took a FULL-PAGE screenshot to see it; the User-Facing Jargon gate had independently gone red on the same text, which is why that release-gate failure existed. Every measurement I took before the fix was taken on the wrong box model and had to be redone. Gate: validate_doctype_first (49 pages, teeth).
FIND 2 — NAVIGATION DESTINATIONS HIDDEN WITH NO CUE, and it is a PLATFORM class, not a page bug. The detail tab strip measured scrollWidth 854 against clientWidth 354: five of eight tabs off-screen, with 'Sign-off' 787px out (more than two screen-widths of swiping) and 'Change orders' — the tab this whole arc hardened — invisible. No fade, no snap, no arrow. The list strip was the same: 260px hidden, 'Complete' and 'All' both entirely off-screen, so a worker on a phone could not reach their finished projects. Swept the pattern platform-wide and found it twice more: analytics' phase tabs hid 'What to do' (the prescriptive phase the page exists to deliver) and its criticality chips hid Medium and Low; community's filter chips hid a category AND set scrollbar-width:none, removing the last cue that the row scrolled.
FIXED by WRAPPING below 640px rather than adding a scroll cue — a cue still asks the user to discover a gesture, and everything is then reachable only if they think to swipe. Desktop behaviour is untouched (verified nowrap + scrollWidth === clientWidth at 1280).
GATED as a 10th Arc W lens (hiddennav_floor) inside the EXISTING arc_w_visual probe rather than a new harness — it already walks every page at 390 and 1280. Counts per hidden DESTINATION, and only for strips whose children are mostly buttons/links: a table or carousel scrolling horizontally is an expected gesture, a row of destinations hiding half of itself is not. Platform now 0 across 25 pages x 2 viewports (headline lens_floor 1 -> 0); baseline banked at 0 with tol 0, and the consistency ceilings tightened while I was there (radius 6->5, combo 40->35). Teeth proven against a synthetic clipped strip, with a scrolling table beside it that the detector correctly ignored.
TAP TARGETS / OVERFLOW: 0 under 44px and 0 real horizontal overflow, in both the list and detail states — but only after correcting the INSTRUMENT twice. It first counted the closed companion widget (scale(0.4), visibility:hidden — a rect still has size) and then the off-canvas feedback drawer, whose 'overflow' was my comparing against innerWidth, which includes the 23px scrollbar, instead of clientWidth. Both would have been false bugs.

PJK1.name: A money decision needs an identity and a trail
PJK1.notes: OPEN on measured ground (2026-07-28). Six of seven project tables have NO auth_uid column at all - only `projects` has one - so raising or approving a CHANGE ORDER, which is a contract amendment, is attributable to nobody. And `projects` appears nowhere in hive_audit_log.target_type while assets, logbook, inventory_items, marketplace_listings, marketplace_sellers, worker_profiles and amc_briefings all do. AHK1 covered an approval DECISION on a forgeable name; here the identity column does not exist and the trail is absent entirely. DETECT COMPLETE 2026-07-28: measured via pg_attribute that auth_uid exists on `projects` ONLY - project_items, project_change_orders, project_progress_logs, project_roles, project_links and project_knowledge have no such column - and via a DISTINCT on hive_audit_log.target_type that `projects` has never written one audit row. The change-order schema makes it concrete: requested_by text NOT NULL and approved_by text, on a row carrying cost_impact_php and schedule_impact_days. project_roles.assigned_by is a text name too. SWEEP/FIX/GATE open. GATE 2026-07-28: validate_change_order_immutability. It asserts the trigger still covers UPDATE AND DELETE (losing DELETE silently restores the make-it-disappear path), that every commercial term is still named in the immutability check (a term quietly dropped from that list becomes editable again - exactly the failure this arc found), that status/approved_by/approved_at/rejection_reason are NOT frozen because freezing them would break the lifecycle the table exists for, and LIVE that the trigger is attached and ENABLED - a disabled trigger looks present and enforces nothing. Teeth proven by unfreezing cost_impact_php: FAIL on exactly that term. STILL OPEN for this class, and stated rather than rounded up: the ATTRIBUTION half. Six of seven project tables still have no auth_uid, and `projects` still writes nothing to hive_audit_log, so a change order is now tamper-EVIDENT-by-construction but still not ATTRIBUTABLE.

PJK2.name: A schedule/health number must be falsifiable
PJK2.notes: OPEN. renderCpm reads _progress.critical_path (item_ids, total_days, slack_per_item) and renderBudget reads _progress.earned_value (bac, pv, and a green/amber/red status), both computed in the project-progress edge fn with no in-repo oracle found at ground. AHK2 governed inspection TIMING; these decide which work may slip and what health a CLIENT is told. EVM has published formulas (CPI=EV/AC, SPI=EV/PV) so the thresholds are checkable against a standard, exactly as AH7's RPN was. CLOSED 2026-07-28 by the PJ7 + PJ8 walks. HALF THE FINDING WAS THAT THE ENGINE IS GOOD, and my ground note claiming otherwise was WRONG and is corrected: prescriptive.py cites PMBOK 7 §6.5.2.2 + AACE 24R-03 and uses networkx.dag_longest_path(); diagnostic.py cites PMBOK 7 + AACE RP 80R-13, states every formula, attributes the bands, and refuses on missing inputs. What was wrong was TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS (the client's uncited EVM copy, already diverging on rounding by up to 0.5% of BAC) and AN ABSENCE RENDERED AS A VERDICT (an unavailable rollup drawing every task as non-critical with zero slack, and a budget pane telling a supervisor to add data that already existed). Both fixed; the EVM contract is registered partial_variant with the honest reason - the FORMULAS are standard, it is AC that is a proxy, and no caller passes the rate override that exists. GATE validate_schedule_health_falsifiable, which also asserts the ENGINE keeps its citations so a future 'simplification' cannot quietly remove them. It strips COMMENTS before hunting the deleted client implementation - its own first run failed because the comment recording the removal quotes the removed code, the third comment-vs-code scanner bug in one session. Teeth proven by reinstating the magic rate in code.

PJK3.name: Authority must be enforced where the data is
PJK3.notes: OPEN. Every project table carries ONE permissive FOR ALL policy whose WITH CHECK tests only hive_id IN user_hive_ids() - so any active member can approve, reject or cancel a change order. project_roles is the only table with a supervisor predicate. Separately, renderBudget refuses non-supervisors in the RENDERER ('Budget visibility is restricted to supervisors') while projects_hive_rw grants every member read - the number is one db.from('projects') away. Sharpens feedback_ui_only_approval_gate_is_bypassable from a button to a whole pane. DETECT COMPLETE 2026-07-28: all seven policies dumped from pg_policy - each is a single PERMISSIVE FOR ALL whose WITH CHECK tests only auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND hive_id IN user_hive_ids(). project_roles_supervisor_all is the ONLY one with a supervisor predicate. So the approve/reject/cancel buttons are gated by nothing but hive membership. Separately renderBudget refuses non-supervisors in the RENDERER while projects_hive_rw grants every member SELECT. SWEEP/FIX/GATE open - the live probe (read the budget as a worker) is the next unit. FIXED + GATED 2026-07-28. Three UI-only claims are now enforced in the DATABASE: the budget (column privileges + a supervisor-only RPC + removed from v_project_truth), project removal (supervisor-gated and audited), and progress-report acknowledgement (supervisor-gated, and no self-acknowledgement). GATE validate_project_authority, and it checks MECHANISMS rather than names - the budget assertion asks information_schema.column_privileges whether `authenticated` still holds SELECT on budget_php, because a column-level REVOKE is a NO-OP while a table-wide GRANT stands and that is precisely how the first attempt failed silently while the page looked fixed. It also refuses a DISABLED trigger (tgenabled <> 'D'), since a disabled trigger looks present and enforces nothing. Teeth proven by re-granting the column: FAIL, with the no-op warning printed inline so the next person does not repeat the mistake.
